transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-26 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SRE), Lena (Bolt ML), Samir (Bolt Infra), Nora (Bolt PM), Tyler (Bolt CTO)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC performance sweep results, focused on TTFT/streaming path, sequence length distribution, and kernel choices. Agreed to run targeted microburst tests and share detailed dumps. Decided to try KV cache toggles and a lightweight quant profile for the 512-seq path.

Topics Covered:
- Current TTFT variability and worst-case microbursts
- Streaming handshake and early-token prioritization
- Sequence-length weighted kernel selection (short vs long kernels)
- KV cache impact and prefix caching strategies
- Next steps and owners

Action items (captured in metadata): see above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jared: okay everyone thanks for joining, um let's do a quick round of where we are, the main aim is to go over the sweep numbers from last night and lock down the next microburst run
[00:14] Lena: yep, thanks Jared. we pulled the sweep overnight, we ran the 128/256/512 buckets, microburst profile at 50 rps - seems like the 512 path is where ttft jumps, and there's a lot more variance
[00:30] Priya: mm-hmm, and just to be clear, when you say ttft jump, do you mean first token latency or time-to-first-token in the streaming stack?
[00:42] Lena: sorry, yes, first token, the streaming handshake plus kernel warmup, looks like median is fine but p95 and p99 spike
[00:56] Marco: one strange thing i saw, sometimes the kernel chooser flips to a long-kernel that isn't quant-friendly which adds 30-40 ms, i think that's our hedging policy colliding with seqlen misclassification
[01:12] Samir: could that be because some requests have trailing prompt length that confuses the sequence estimator, we do pre-truncation but maybe mismatch in how Redwood estimates the required kv allocation
[01:27] Priya: yep, exactly. our estimator uses the request's declared max tokens + prefix heuristics, but if the client sends a streaming init without the full prompt we sometimes conservatively pick long-kernel. we can tweak to use observed initial chunk to favor short-kernel for first token
[01:47] Tyler: would that risk quality or generate errors? we can't have hallucinations or cutoff.
[01:54] Priya: it shouldn't affect quality, it's only a kernel execution path change; we still reserve the full KV, just choose a faster kernel for the early token and then switch to the long-kernel as we see the rest of the sequence. there's a small overhead to switching but it buys you 20-40ms on ttft
[02:12] Nora: what about caching? we saw a note in the README about prefix caching, how do we measure its effect on p95?
[02:21] Jared: good point, Priya ran experiments with KV cache on vs off - Priya, can you share the numbers?
[02:29] Priya: sure, quick summary: with prefix/KV cache enabled we saw median improve 10-12ms and p95 drop by about 18-22ms for 128/256. for 512 the benefit is still positive but less predictable due to cache misses on long prefixes and on cross-request cache invalidation in our test harness
[02:49] Lena: in our workload many sessions have long prompts with retrieval augmentation so cache hit ratio is like 38% which explains the smaller win on bigger seqs
[03:01] Marco: another wrinkle is microburst concurrency: when we simulate bursts of 80 concurrent streaming sessions the scheduler does coalescing which helps throughput but increases tail due to contention on kernel loading
[03:18] Samir: do you have a breakdown — is that contention on device transfer, or kernel jitting, or CUDA stream serialization?
[03:26] Marco: mostly kernel selection + CUDA stream stalls, a few calls hit a cold quant path and also trigger a slower matmul kernel that we saw in the trace
[03:36] Priya: note: we have an optimization where we pre-warm popular kernels during pen testing, we can try a focused pre-warm for the 512 featureset during the microburst run
[03:48] Tyler: pre-warming sounds good but will increase baseline GPU cycles - we need to weigh cost vs unit latency gains
[03:55] Jared: yep that's the cost/latency tradeoff the thesis here, Redwood can propose two profiles: conservative (no pre-warm, cheaper) and burst-optimized (pre-warm + more threads, higher cost but lower p99)
[04:10] Lena: can you quantify the cost uplift? we need an estimate to bring back to finance
[04:15] Jared: we'll put numbers in the perf dump. rough ballpark from past pilots is 7-12% more GPU time for the pre-warm profile under our simulated bursts
[04:27] Nora: any thought on quantization? we tried a 4-bit quant on a separate run and saw small quality drift but latency improved notably on some kernels
[04:36] Priya: yes, quant profile Q4-lite reduces matmul latency on the long-kernel path by ~25ms in ideal cases, but switching cost and occasional dequantization edge-cases made it risky for all traffic. we typically recommend canarying quant on low-risk routes first
[04:52] Samir: do you have tooling to run traffic-split canaries while capturing token-level quality metrics?
[04:58] Priya: we do — Redwood telemetry ties tokens to eval sets, you can run a sampling config at 5-10% and we collect token loss / rouge-ish proxies and compare against baseline
[05:12] Lena: nice. for Bolt, we want to run quant only on the assistant-short route where seqlen < 200 and keep long retrieval routes on fp16
[05:22] Jared: ok makes sense. quick note on hedging: we tested fallback to a cheaper model variant during capacity spikes; it worked but introduced slight style differences — something to monitor
[05:36] Tyler: style drift is important to product. If fallback changes phrasing we need QA sign-off
[05:41] Priya: we can include a golden prompt set to check style drift during canaries
[05:47] Marco: regarding kernel chooser, i want to propose that we add a lightweight seqlen predictor hook at enqueue time that looks at the first 64 tokens seen in streaming init and biases kernel selection to short-path; if the stream grows we flip to long-path on the next scheduling tick
[06:06] Samir: sounds reasonable as long as the flip is cheap. what about state migration cost?
[06:11] Priya: the migration is basically moving to the long kernel with a small memcpy, we've measured it 8-12ms in prior tests
[06:19] Nora: what's the net benefit then? if you save 30ms on first token but pay 10ms to switch, net is 20ms which is worthwhile
[06:26] Jared: exactly. it's a net win for customer-facing metrics that care about TTFT
[06:31] [07:00] --- (skipping to microburst results section) ---
[07:05] Priya: okay microburst dump: with the kernel-bias patch, first-token median for 512 went from 210ms to 185ms, p95 from 480ms to 398ms, p99 from 780 to 640 in this run. caveat: the run had a lower cache hit rate than your production hist but still directionally promising
[07:30] Lena: nice improvement. what did you do about hedging timeouts?
[07:34] Priya: we increased the early-token timeout from 80ms to 120ms for streaming init in that test to avoid premature fallbacks, that reduced unnecessary model switching but slightly increased median in non-burst windows
[07:50] Marco: we also toggled CUDA stream priorities in one run, giving early-token paths higher priority lowered worst tails but increased jitter overall; tradeoff there
[08:03] Samir: can we get the raw flamegraph or the trace log? we want to map back to our infra triggers
[08:08] Priya: yes, we'll upload the full trace and a condensed waterfall CSV; Jared will share link
[08:15] Jared: sharing note: expects link in chat after call — and the perf dump will include p95/p99 broken down by kernel name
[08:23] Nora: on the business side, timeline wise, Bolt needs to decide on pilot rollforward by Sept 10th, we have budget review on the 12th so the perf numbers feed into that
[08:34] Jared: understood; we'll prioritize the 512 microburst run and the KV cache A/B to get those numbers in time
[08:40] Tyler: curious about storage of logs — we need audit logs and retention controls; does Redwood support per-customer retention and purge?
[08:48] Marco: briefly, yes, we support configurable retention and can push logs to your S3 or GCS with server-side encryption; for PII we recommend edge-filtering at the customer side then send redacted transcripts
[09:02] Lena: we'll follow up with security on the exact retention window. Samir, will you take point?
[09:07] Samir: yes, will do.
[09:09] [09:30] --- (wrap-up and recap) ---
[09:32] Jared: quick recap — Redwood: run focused microburst for seqlen 512, run KV-cache A/B, upload traces and cost delta for pre-warm profile; Bolt: share seqlen histogram and infra limits, schedule SRE review; timeline end of week for perf dumps, Sept 6 for SRE deep-dive
[09:53] Lena: sounds good. small ask: can Priya include the exact kernel mapping so our engineers can triage quickly?
[09:59] Priya: yes, will include kernel names and the conditions that triggered them in the dump
[10:05] Nora: thanks everyone, appreciate the prioritization
[10:08] Jared: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and the next meeting invite
[10:12] (end)
